lines.text: Well, today is officially the worst day of my life.
I just got fired from my job.
And on top of that, my boyfriend decided to break up with me.
Wait, what's this? A letter? Maybe some good news for a change?
Oh my, it's from my dear old grandfather. He asks to visit him urgently. What happened?
I have no choice but to go visit him.
So, leaving my city life behind, I'm embarking on a journey to a place filled with memories from my childhood. Who knows what awaits me there?

locations.title: Cafe
locations.story: Emily returns to her hometown after receiving a mysterious letter from her grandfather. She encounters unexpected challenges and meets new and old friends.

locations.title: Cafe Facade
locations.story: Emily decides to restore the cafe's facade to make it more appealing to guests.

locations.title: Kitchen
locations.story: Emily's finding even more of Grandpa's recipe pieces. She decides to collect the remaining pieces no matter what, but Aunt Mei shares some disturbing news with her...

locations.title: Guestroom
locations.story: Time's ticking before the food critic pays Emily a visit, and she still doesn't have the full recipe. Little does Emily know that more serious problems await her.

locations.title: Garden
locations.story: No one's heard from Grandpa, and Emily is now the legal heir of both the family cafe and the family debts. She's looking for a way to make more money.

locations.title: Food Truck
locations.story: Emily has a stroke of luck and now has a chance to participate in the town fair. She hopes the abandoned food truck she restored will help her win the grand prize. But is it really abandoned?

locations.title: Beach Bar
locations.story: It looks like the debt's been taken care of, and Emily can finally breathe a sigh of relief. The secret prize at the fair was a rundown beach bar. Emily and her friends are enjoying their time and deciding what to do with the prize.

locations.title: Cabinet
locations.story: Thanks to an unexpected lead, Emily and Olivia discover their grandfather's office, where they hope to find information about his disappearance. Emily will also have to dig into her past.

locations.title: Art Studio
locations.story: Shortly before his disappearance, Grandpa used money he borrowed to buy a space he intended to turn into an art studio to surprise Emily. But it looks like he didn't manage to pull off his surprise, so Emily will have to restore the space herself.

locations.title: Music Studio
locations.story: The owner of the music studio next door asks Emily to help her organize it in exchange for details about Emily's grandfather's disappearance.

locations.title: Flower Shop
locations.story: Emily finally knows why her grandfather disappeared, but she still doesn't know where he is. Aunt Mei invites Emily to help at the flower shop, which has fallen on hard times.

locations.title: Spa
locations.story: Emily visits an abandoned house tied to her grandfather's past. As she helps restore it, she uncovers a story of rivalry, love, and loss.

locations.title: Forest Cabin
locations.story: Emily stumbles upon an old cabin full of childhood memories. While restoring it, she finds hidden letters that reveal more about her grandfather's past. Could this place hold the answers she seeks?

locations.title: Night Fair
locations.story: A date at a strangely unsettling night fair turns into a restoration project where eerie events trouble Emily, but Joe remains skeptical until a mysterious figure appears.

locations.title: Fate Wagon
locations.story: Emily seeks answers in the fortune teller's caravan, but an unusual ritual takes a chaotic turn. What begins as playful curiosity soon stirs something far more serious - and maybe even dangerous.

locations.title: Lighthouse
locations.story: Drawn by a cryptic clue, Emily arrives at a forgotten lighthouse. As shadows deepen and a storm rages outside, she realizes she might not be the only one here.

locations.title: Boathouse
locations.story: At the old pier, Emily discovers a boat that could change the course of her journey.

locations.title: Island
locations.story: Grandpa faces new challenges far from home, where humor and resilience keep hope alive.

locations.title: Backyard
locations.story: A quiet day at Aunt Mei's backyard turns into a cheerful family project filled with laughter and good stories.

locations.title: Italian Restaurant
locations.story: Emily joins Enzo to restore a new restaurant, only to find that some things are harder to fix than broken walls.

locations.title: Editorial Office
locations.story: Emily rushes to help Felix after his office is left in ruins. As they clean up the mess, a newly discovered hidden archive hints that this was no ordinary break-in.

locations.title: Pool
locations.story: Emily helps Enzo bring his pool back to life. Before anyone can relax by the water, there's plenty of work to dive into.

lines.message: Oh, boy. I've really gotta work on this place.
My goodness!
Are you OK?
I meant to do that!
Who are you, and what are you doing here?
I'd like to ask you the same thing!
I'm Emily. This family cafe belongs to my grandfather. I don't really know why it's in this shape... What about you?
I was just walking along nearby, looking for something interesting. This place seemed abandoned, so I decided to take a look inside.
My name's Olivia. I got really pretty hungry, and since this is a cafe... I thought I might be able to find something to eat here.
I could make something to eat, if you don't mind. How about a couple of sandwiches?
That would be great!
Emily, those sandwiches were amazing!
I'm glad you liked them.
I thought I'd tidy up while you were making the food.
That's really nice of you.
No, I completely forgot! I've got to run. I hope we see each other again!
Odd... I wonder what happened to her.
Aunt Mei? Is that really you?
My goodness, Emily. You're all grown up!
I can't believe that it's really you, Aunt Mei! I missed you.
I've missed you too, dear. It's been so long since we last saw each other.
Aunt Mei, I received a letter from grandfather. Do you know anything about it?
A letter? Well... Maybe. Your grandfather said something about it.
But I don't remember what exactly. I wasn't ever sure I understood him...
Aunt Mei, take a look at the letter. It might refresh your memory.
Oh, Emily... Now I get it. Your grandfather always had a plan.
What plan, Aunt Mei? Please tell me.
Your grandfather left a will, just in case something happened to him.
It should be somewhere here in the cafe.
But you can't find it in all this mess...
Oh! What fell out of the letter?
Look, Aunt Mei! It's a mystery from grandfather.
Your grandfather loved riddles.
That sounds like him! Maybe there are more puzzle pieces hidden in the cafe?
I hope you're right and that's really the case.
Sorry, Emily, I'll leave you for a bit. See you!
Olivia, you're back! What do you have there?
I found this old book with pictures. It's got a lot of notes in it, but I can't make heads or tails of it.
Where did you find it?! This is a recipe book that belonged to my grandfather.
He wouldn't just leave it lying around like that. Can I take a closer look at it?
I can't say "no" after those delicious sandwiches of yours.
Oh no... The page with the signature cherry pie recipe has been completely ripped out.
What was so important about that page?
That cherry pie recipe was grandfather's pride and joy. I think I've already found one of the recipe pieces.
Olivia, look! I was right! It was a piece of the page with the cherry pie recipe.
Where do you think the other pieces are?
I wish I knew...
Oh! Is that the telephone? I didn't know there was a telephone here.
Hello?
Emily, it's me again, your Aunt Mei. Could I ask you for a favor?
Aunt Mei, of course. How can I help you?
Well, my granddaughter is visiting me, and I'd like to offer her something nice to eat.
I thought since the cafe's working again, it would be nice to support you by ordering something.
Of course! What does she like?
She's got a sweet tooth, so how about a cake?
Consider it done, Aunt Mei. I'll make sure it's the best cake she's ever tried!
You're a lifesaver, Emily. I'll pop in soon to pick it up. Thank you!
You can count on me, Aunt Mei. See you soon!
Did you find something, Olivia?
Yes, there's another recipe piece here.
You've got hawk eyes!
Haha, I know.
That means grandfather really did hide recipe pieces here in the cafe.
I'm now one step closer to the whole recipe!
Olivia, why don't you help me look for the recipe? We could uncover the secret of making the most delicious cherry pie ever!
Thanks, Emily, but I'm hunting for real treasures.
I'm not sure the recipe is what I'm looking for.
Do you know what you're passing on? You could enjoy the most delicious pie you've ever tasted. It's worth the adventure!
The most delicious? Sounds tempting. Maybe I won't be so stubborn...
Take your time to think about it. The pie recipe might have more emotions in store for you than you expect.
It's a really tempting offer, but I really have to think about it.
Today was an eventful day!
I met Olivia and saw Aunt Mei. The cafe's running again, and I'm on my way to solving the mystery of the disappearance of grandfather and his signature recipe.
I think tomorrow will have new encounters and challenges for me. I'm ready for them!
This place holds so many memories and dreams.
The outer appearance should attract guests. It's not likely to attract anyone in this state. I need to fix that right away.
This sign spoils the appearance. It's time to take it down!
Oh, no! Not that!
Whoever you are, thank you so much for catching me! You're a lifesaver!
Hi, Emily! Long time no see.
Joe? Is it really you? What a surprise!
I'm happy to see you, too.
We haven't seen each other in forever!
What brings you back?
It's a long story...
As you can see, I'm back and trying to restore the cafe's previous appearance.
And what have you been doing all this time?
You know, I haven't wasted any time either.
I've learned a lot about carpentry and repairs over the past few years.
You must be a real handyman!
I think you might be overestimating me, Emily, but thanks. Do you need help with the cafe?
Oh, that's sweet! I definitely won't manage everything on my own, and I really need someone I can rely on right now.
Do you mean me? Thanks, Em. You can count on me!
By the way, I was just about to throw away this old sign. It's seen better days.
If you don't mind, I can restore it to its former glory.
Joe, I really appreciate your help. It won't be too much trouble for you? You probably have other things to do.
Don't worry about that, Emily.
I'll take the sign back to my workshop.
I'm looking forward to seeing you again!
I hope I wasn't too pushy.
Well, well, well. What have we here?
Another lousy cafe trying to compete with my places?
Excuse me?!
Where are my manners? Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Enzo, and I'm the owner of a local fast-food chain.
I'm here to help you avoid making the biggest mistake of your life.
What are you talking about?
This town doesn't need another failed business.
I suggest you save yourself the trouble and close up the cafe before you embarrass yourself.
I think there's been a misunderstanding. I didn't open a new cafe.
This place is my family's legacy. My grandfather used to own it, and now I do.
What? You inherited this sad little cafe?
Yes, this cafe now belongs to me, and it'll soon be ready for another grand opening.
We'll see about that, little girl.
Well, that was rude and unexpected. I didn't expect such a "warm welcome".
It's strange, though. He seemed familiar.
His resemblance to Joe... Could it be just a coincidence?
I guess my imagination's just playing tricks on me.
Next time, I won't let him speak to me in such a contemptuous tone.
How are you, Em? I decided to take a break at the workshop and come see you.
Everything alright here?
Everything's just fine. But something strange happened.
An odd man came back and was really arrogant.
Wow, you don't see that too often in our town. What did he say to you?
He made it clear he doesn't want any competition with his establishments.
His name is Enzo. Have you ever heard of him?
Yeah, he's pretty well-known in town. He's a local businessman.
Let's just say his tactics are pretty aggressive, and he doesn't take kindly to any new places threatening his monopoly.
Really?! That explains his behavior. It felt like he was ready to crush anybody who got in his way.
But he seemed familiar as if I'd seen him somewhere before.
Maybe it's just a coincidence.
There are a lot of guys like him, so maybe you've met someone similar. These mean monopolists are all the same.
I guess so. It just caught me off guard.
In any case, thanks, Joe. For your help and everything. It means a lot to me.
Of course, Em. It's time to go back to the workshop. See you!
What do we have here?
Another recipe piece. That wasn't the most obvious of places.
I hope the others aren't hidden as well.
Hey, Emily! How are you holding up? I heard about your run-in with Enzo. It probably wasn't fun, was it?
Yeah, he was incredibly rude. Do you know anything about him, Aunt Mei? He seemed oddly familiar.
Enzo's story is complicated. He used to be a close friend of mine, but that was in the past.
What happened?
It's a long story, but let's just say he made a difficult decision that led him to where he is today.
He became more focused on his own success and lost sight of what really mattered.
That's sad.
It's true, Emily. Sometimes, people have to sacrifice a lot to achieve success.
I wanted to tell you something.
You probably noticed the resemblance between Enzo and Joe. That's what you meant?
I did. They have similar features. Are they related?
Yes. Enzo is Joe's father.
What?! I had a strange feeling, but I didn't expect that!
Now, it makes sense why Joe didn't want to answer when I asked him about Enzo. He never said anything about his father in the past.
They have a complicated relationship, Emily. Joe has his reasons for keeping his ties to Enzo hidden.
Reasons? How could he hide something so important from me? I was wrong to trust him.
Emily, he probably didn't want to burden you with his family issues.
I understand your disappointment, Emily. Maybe you should discuss this with Joe. I mean, you guys aren't strangers.
I guess you're right, Aunt Mei. One way or another, we'll definitely have this conversation. I can't keep it to myself.
I hope I'm on time. Em, I finished the sign.
Joe, you're just in time!
We were just talking about you.
I hope it was something good.
Almost. Aunt Mei told me something about Enzo. Is there anything you want to tell me?
Emily... I didn't want you to find out like this, but I guess you already know that Enzo is my father.
I'm not proud of his behavior, but I thought it would be easier for both of us.
For us or for you? Joe...
I thought it wasn't the right moment.
Emily, Joe isn't like his father. You see that, right?
Thank you, Mei. Emily, I'm deeply sorry for my father's actions.
Joe, you saved me and helped me with the sign. We've known each other for a long time, but you never told me about your dad. I'd like to think my trust in you is reciprocal...
I think you can manage without me, lovebirds. I have to go!
Joe! What are you doing? Helping our competitors?
Father, I don't see anything wrong with that. Emily is my friend, and I volunteered to help her.
Friends won't pay your bills.
Focus on our business, not this insignificant venture.
It's not just about money, Father. This cafe means a lot to Emily.
Means a lot. You're so naive. You're flushing your potential down the drain, Joe. They're just using you.
I believe in Emily. She'll make it. You should be more polite to her.
We'll see about that. Your father wouldn't say no to a little help. You won't deny me that, will you?
My God! I didn't expect that...
And now I'm alone again. I guess I'll have to hang the sign myself.
My journey continues, and I'm excited to see what lies ahead.
Now's definitely not the time to back down.
It's amazing how much I've already done.
In such a short time, we've managed to breathe new life into this cafe.
There's still a lot to do, but the cafe reminds me of something from my memories. My grandfather would be proud of me.
Hmm... Judging by the map, I'm in the right spot. It should be around here somewhere.
Olivia! What are you doing here?
Oh! Emily, I didn't know you were here. I, um... I'm looking for something.
Can I help you find it? Are you looking for something specific?
I didn't want to share this information with anybody.
Now, I've got to loop you in since you've already seen me here.
I found this treasure map, and I couldn't resist following the route on it. It led me here.
A treasure map? Can I see it?
This map... It's the same one my grandfather made for me when I was your age, Olivia.
He and I used to go treasure hunting for fun.
So, I'm too late? That's not fair!
I'm sorry, Olivia, but it seems that way. But that was many years ago.
Why am I so unlucky? I didn't expect to walk away empty-handed.
You know, Olivia, since you're here, how about we make a deal?
I could use some help in the kitchen, and in return, I'll treat you to something delicious.
Delicious, huh? I'm pretty hungry. I won't budge here until I get something nice to eat right now!
I have a treat for you. But maybe we should clean up a little first?
Alright, fine. I'll help you. I hope the treat is worth it!
You won't be disappointed.
Great job, Olivia! You're an awesome helper.
Thank you, Emily!

Agre-
-ed.

... That's not the point.

Joe?..

This is really suspicious. We should stay alert.
Let me know if you see anything else.
Maybe I'm just tired, and I really did imagine it?
Bzzzt... tr-r-r... ding.
What was that? What kind of sound is that?
I think it came from here.
What is that device? A fortune-telling machine?
Why did it suddenly turn on by itself?
Hmm, it shut off. Looks like it's broken.
Just like everything here. I wonder who owns all this.
I'm more interested in why it's all in such a state.
Who could let such a promising place fall apart like this?
Emily, did you notice something? What are you thinking about?
Did you notice that the fog lifted as soon as the machine turned off?
What? How did I miss that?
Maybe it's just a coincidence - otherwise it all feels way too mystical.
I don't believe in mysticism. There has to be a logical explanation.
And did you notice there's nobody here but us? How could the machine turn on by itself?
We should take a closer look around.
Nothing suspicious, but it's still deserted - no one around.
It's still strange. That figure in the window.
If it was the owner, they'd have shown up by now.
You're right. We've been here for quite a while.
Heh. Maybe they're waiting for us to clean everything up so they can show up to a finished job?
I think someone's coming.
Get behind me and stay alert.
Hey there, kids.
Well, great - didn't let me finish my sentence. Why are you two so tense?
Oh, it's you.
Good to see you. You're the first people we've seen in this place everyone forgot.
It's not forgotten.
We remember it - after all, we're the ones who told Joe about it.
From the way you described it, it wasn't this run-down. What are you doing here?
We're here to...
...put it back in order.
So you're the owners?
Who would've thought.
Yeah, we're the owners. Cool place, huh?
Well, not exactly us.
And it's not that cool.
Joe, come on. You said yourself it was a promising place.
Wait - was it you in that window, watching us?
What? What window?
My brother wouldn't even fit in a window that small.
What did you say?
Easy, easy, guys. Something strange is going on here.
Did you say something strange is going on here?
What do you mean? So far, the only strange thing we see is your behavior.
The fair looks abandoned, but at the same time it feels like someone is here.
A ghost?
You know they don't exist.
Oh, they definitely do.
I highly doubt it. But if there really are ghosts here, they'll hurt our business.
Business? What are you planning?
We already said it.
We want to bring this place back to life.
And make money off it.
That too - no point pretending otherwise.
I see you brought materials with you. What's your plan?
In the plan we...
...disagree a little.
I want to open the carousel.
A waste of time, bro.
And why is that?
Because all the attention will be on my shooting range.
The carousel is the heart of any fair. Since when is a shooting range the center?
Nonsense. That old carousel is useless.
I thought the center of any fair was the Ferris wheel.
Yeah, I think so too.
Many people are afraid of heights, so the carousel is the choice of the majority.
You wanted to say "shooting gallery" - the choice of the majority.
We can only prove it in practice.
The only smart thing you've said in a while.
This rivalry is going to be legendary.
Ha! You sure you're restoring things and not breaking them?
Don't talk while I'm working - mind your own business.
Let me help you, Frank. I've got a lot of experience with restoration and repairs.
I won't say no to help, buddy.
What? What about fair competition?
Then I'll help you, Philip. That seems fair.
Well that's unexpected - I thought you'd help us.
It's fairer if I help Philip, since you volunteered to help Frank.
So it's a competition?
Only if it's friendly.
Friendly? I thought this was a date.
Hehe. Back to work. May the best team win.
You're doing pretty well. You're strong competitors.
Hey, I thought you were on my team.
Thanks, Joe. You're doing great too.
But we'll definitely finish faster.
We competing speed?
I think you two get along way too well for rivals.
Yeah, I noticed too. Are we even competing here?
We are. We just don't forget to enjoy the process.
Is there any other way?
Wait - so is this a competition between us, or between you two?
Because right now it looks like you just found an excuse to spend time together.
I don't see anything wrong with that.
Honestly, we're mostly trying to keep you two from completely falling out.
Well, I don't know - I feel like the third wheel.
Me too.
But at least the competition stays fair.
And really fun.
We're keeping a good pace. If we keep it up, we've got a real shot at winning.
Things are going according to plan on our side too.
We're already celebrating victory.
"Don't count your chickens before they hatch."
I'll admit, you work fast. But we're trying not to fall behind.
Makes it more exciting to see who finishes first.
It seems that we are really competing for speed.
Yeeaah! We won!
You did great, Frank.
Couldn't have done it without you, Joe. We're a great team.
Nooo, that can't be.
Emily, you were totally going easy on him.
I was not going easy. We were ahead - I don't know how this happened.
And anyway, shouldn't visitors decide with their wallets who wins?
Don't be upset, bro. People will appreciate the carousel.
You...
Easy, Philip. We need to finish the shooting range so the competition can really begin.
I thought it already ended.
And... we're done.
This is pointless now. My brother will remind me of this competition forever.
Oh, absolutely.
You two did great. Your shooting range looks amazing.
Thanks, Joe. You were worthy opponents.
But the win is still ours.
So what was the prize anyway? You never agreed on one.
For me, the main prize is a great time. Thanks everyone for taking part.
Tr-r-r... click... ding.
What's it? Ghosts? It's true... We can't be here.
Bro, where are you going? It's just a fortune-telling machine.
Sorry - he's very superstitious. I need to catch up with him and make sure he doesn't do anything stupid.
Who would've thought Frank was such a scaredy-cat.
And Philip is so caring.
Is this happening again? Why now?
Joe, there's a figure in the window again.
You're right. Sorry I didn't believe you earlier. Looks like that figure really is watching us.
Do you think it's connected to the fortune machine?
This time the machine printed a prediction. Let's see what it says.
It says: soon the path will lead you to someone who's been waiting for a meeting for a long time.
How mysterious. I want to try getting a prediction.
Emily, you don't actually believe this stuff, do you? It's just tricks and gimmicks.
I know. Fortunes are always written so they fit any situation.
But I'm curious what this machine will give me.
I think I broke it.
I don't think it's your fault. It was already broken.
Joe, the figure in the window is gone again.
Whoever that mysterious figure is, I don't like them.
Do you remember the prediction? Maybe it really is true, and someone is desperate to meet us.
I don't know, Emily. Let's stay alert and get rid of this weird thing. It doesn't belong at the fair.
What if we try to fix it?
Iron only whispers what someone put into it.
True signs don't need wires and gears.
The young man is right - the fair doesn't need empty promises.
No machine can replace a person. Especially in my craft.
Metal can repeat, but it can't feel.
I've been watching you here for a long time.
Watching us?
The fair rarely responds to outsiders, and you made it stir.
I couldn't help but appear when you paid attention to that machine.
I told you someone was watching us. Were you the one in that window?
Maybe.
You're looking for what slipped away from you, but it still hasn't lost its echo.
You mean my grandpa? Can you really help me?
Help comes to those who aren't afraid to take a step toward it.
But words need a home to be heard.
A home?
My wagon - an old office on wheels. Without it, the signs stay mute.
Help me bring it here, and then answers may find their way.
Come in. Time doesn't like waiting.
Can we at least introduce ourselves?
Names matter where there is no magic.
You already know who I am. It was you who called out to me.
Are you a fortune teller...
Fate itself brought us together. The night does not wait. Are you ready to find answers to the questions that torment you?
I want to try. Maybe it really will help.
Are you that sure?
Yes.
Okay, then I'll be with you.
Make yourselves at home, young people.
And don't mind the mess.
We're used to it.
Yeah. I'd be surprised if we found this place tidy.
Agreed. That would be real magic.
The chaos here is no accident.
In my craft, things must be placed so they don't interfere with the signs... and so prying eyes don't read more than they're allowed.
Sounds like an excuse.
Don't joke about magic, young man.
Joe, please. We came here for help.
If this really helps us find grandfather, we should try.
I'll need your help preparing for the ritual.
And that help is, of course, cleaning?
What exactly do we need for the ritual... and how will it go? I need to know what to expect.
Everything in its own time, child. First - the place. Then - the request. And only then does what answers the call appear.
Why do you address us so... condescendingly?
Joe...
Time. Next to it, we all sound equally young.
More riddles... Maybe you could share a couple of secrets about our town instead?
I'm afraid your mind isn't ready yet.
Ah. Of course.
My path has been long and thorny.
But in you I sense... a certain strength, young man.
Does Joe have abilities too?
I mean physical strength. He can be trusted with the hardest work - if he truly wants to be useful.
Well, Joe - look where your skepticism got you.
For once... I actually agree with her.
You have no idea how lucky you are.
What do you mean?
Maybe today is the day. No - tonight.
What night?
It's fate, no other way. Tonight, many things are falling into place.
Even I'm intrigued now.
Please, don't keep us in suspense - tell us.
Sorry - just thinking out loud. I hope I didn't scare you.
Do you do this often?
Only when fate's scales offer a surprise like tonight. Nights like this are rare.
Still - what night is it, and why is it so important to you?
Not to me... to you. Tonight is the best night to ask questions - and receive answers.
Seems like an ordinary day to me.
Night.
Correct, child. Night is the time of silence, when signs become clear.
Silence lets you hear what is hidden - and what affects each of us.
Signs are the voice of the wind, the whisper of grass... but the brightest signs are the stars.
They're just celestial bodies.
You're right, young man.
Bodies. And it is their light that points out our path in life and illuminates what we should do next. Don't underestimate their influence.
Amazing... the couch is in surprisingly good condition.
You're right. Whoever made it did solid work.
Hah - it's my most recent purchase. It hasn't had time to wear out yet.
When the magic begins, you'll be truly amazed.
And we're almost at the threshold. Just a little more - and the night will start answering.
Will we need anything else for the ritual?
Everything we need... the night will provide.
The answers have never been closer. The gates are about to open.
If it's gates, do we need a key? Or maybe to pick a lock?
You're thinking correctly, young man. But I still sense... ironic skepticism in you.
The child wondered what the ritual would require.
And you said the night would provide everything we need.
So there are additional requirements now?
I underestimated your companion's skepticism.
For the ritual to succeed, we will need faith - all the faith we have within us.
Faith in what?
Faith in success.
Spirits do not tolerate uncertainty. You must not show them a crack - they will find it.
You can't weaken. Not for a moment.
Wait - spirits?
That's... really unexpected. I guess I should've seen it coming.
We've come to the beginning. Everything is ready, and we are waiting for someone to answer our call.
Does this item look familiar to you?
It's a Luigi board for communicating with otherworldly entities.
I thought it was a board game.
Joe, please be serious - at least out of respect for our host. We're guests here.
Sorry, Emily. I'll try to behave.
I'm used to it. Doubt often enters first, but faith often follows behind it.
May I ask...
Yes, child - ask. But be careful with questions, so no one else hears them.
Why do we need a board to speak with otherworldly entities?
We will try asking your grandfather directly.
Do you think he...
Emily...
I know how hard this is, child. But we must check.
I'm sorry... this is too much. I don't know if I'm ready for the answer.
I'm with you, Emily.
I... I think I feel...
We have guests, child. Formulate your question - quickly. We don't have much time.
Hold on, Emily.
I don't know what to ask...
Phrase it so we can interpret it clearly. Guests won't stay with us all night.
Grandfather... is that you?
No... something's wrong. This shouldn't have happened.
Something's wrong? Did I ask the wrong question?
No, child. Your question was clear and precise... but the answer raises questions.
What was that noise when everything went out?
A guest spoke to us. Our call was heard - and now we have an answer.
Don't keep me hanging... was it my grandfather?
I'm not entirely sure. But relatives from that world don't behave like that.
So what do we do now? That was our ghostly chance to find grandfather.
There is another way. Time is a capricious ally - we must hurry.
Sorry to interrupt... I've been here for a while and I don't understand what's going on.
Philip? I think I know what that noise was.
A new guest? Quickly - help us.
We need to remove the items from the last ritual so no new guests answer the call.
What did I get myself into...
Philip, thanks for the help. How long were you watching us?
Since you lit the candles. It caught my attention.
It's unusual to see you alone. What are you doing here? And where is your brother?
I was looking for him and saw this wagon at the fair. I decided to peek inside, and something strange was happening.
I... I guess I interrupted you. Sorry.
I don't think this is your fault.
And our host has another idea for how we can find grandfather.
So it's about your grandfather... I could've guessed. You chose an unusual method.
It happened by chance - like fate itself arranged it.
It was nothing but fate. You're right, child. It brought us together.
I'm ready to continue. We must quickly create the right atmosphere for a new session.
Please do that without me. I need to find my good-for-nothing brother.
Dear guest, I can help with that after we're prepared.
I think I'll try to handle it myself. But thanks. Good luck, guys.
Good luck to you too, Philip.
Paths rarely diverge forever. If fate brought you together here, it will find a reason to bring you together again.
Emily, can I talk to you alone?
It's important.
Of course, Joe. But remember - we have to hurry.
You asked me to take all this more seriously.
Yeah... is something wrong?
The ritual.
What about the ritual? We got an answer.
We already knew it. Or rather - we hoped for it.
You're right... But our host has another idea.
Our host... doesn't it bother you that we don't even know her name?
She seems very suspicious to me. And that ritual...
What are you trying to say, Joe?
I think it's all a con. And they're just using us to clean this place up.
But Joe... all the signs, the curtains, the candles - she really has a gift.
I think it's just coincidence.
How?
Philip made a draft when he came into the wagon. That explains the torn curtains and the candles.
And the cracked board?
A trick.
I don't want to discuss this right now. We have little time - we need to make it before the night ends.
I know how important this is to you. But you can't lose your head either.
Joe, I don't want to continue this conversation right now.
You've gone quiet... Silence can be louder than noise.
I don't like it when people argue in silence.
We're... just tired. Please don't mind it.
Tiredness comes in many forms, child. One is cured by sleep, another - by truth.
Right now I want only one truth, and it's about my grandfather.
Let's focus on preparing for the new session, okay?
Yeah. Let's... work.
The night won't wait for you to agree with each other.
I sense you want to ask something, child.
Aren't you a fortune-teller?
I try to avoid fixed roles. Who knows what role fate will bring me tomorrow.
The Luigi board is a medium's tool.
As always, the child is right.
Let's say... I'm a medium, but only part-time.
I have many talents. Who knows what role you'll see me in tomorrow if fate brings us together again.
That's a little scary.
Child, what a wonderful table you've chosen.
Joe picked it.
The young man has excellent taste.
What can I say - it is what it is.
Have you ever wondered why the color purple is so closely tied to esotericism?
Purple is often associated with magic and all that esoteric stuff. It's about intuition and "something spiritual".
It's like it sits between hot red and deep blue - so it's seen as a symbol of balance: opposites meeting and holding steady.
Joe... that's unexpected. Where did you learn all that?
I don't know. It just came out.
Probably from keeping silent for too long.
Ha.
I told you - the young man hides a strength within him.
You're embarrassing me.
No, no, no... I think lighting will be unnecessary here.
It ruins the atmosphere.
I actually think this lighting fits perfectly here. And besides...
Didn't you say light shows us the way?
Using my own weapon against me, child...
You can rely on Emily. She has a lot of experience in decorating.
And what's that? Is there someone inside?
That's my assistant and partner.
Can I take a look?
First we'll lay out the divination tools, child. The night is coming to an end, and we must begin the session soon.
A raven?
He has such a tired look...
Ha. Guess he doesn't like us.
Nothing of the sort. That's just his face.
He will help us get a more accurate reading.
A bird?
Not just a bird. He has a noble lineage, and he is my conduit of power.
I can't tell you every detail, so just take my word for it.
Everything is ready for the session. Child, look into the crystal ball and think of your grandfather - and the ball will answer.
Will it be a place? Or more signs and riddles?
Young man, I need you to focus on the ball as well - and on your partner. It will strengthen the ball.
I'll try.
When I speak the spell, the child may ask her question.
I'm beginning.
Night that sees what is hidden...
Stars that remember the roads...
Let the fog gather in a circle, and let the glass become a window.
Show not a word - but a place. Not a dream - but a trace.
Give a sign to the one who seeks.
Where should I look for my grandfather?
The ball has answered us.
A lighthouse... I think it's the town one. The one we saw at the beach.
I don't know any other lighthouses in our town.
We need to go there right away.
Look deeper. It's not just a lighthouse.
What do you mean?
A lighthouse is a symbol of loneliness. It's a sign.
I'm afraid, child, you'll have to go there alone.
What? It could be dangerous.
No reason to worry. A lighthouse is also a symbol of light - a path.
A lighthouse always helps those who are lost find their way.
I'm going there immediately.
Emily, please be careful. And contact me as soon as you can.
Okay, Joe. Don't worry - I can handle it.
You know I'll be...
I know. See you soon.
Paths only seem to diverge. Fate loves circles - and will bring you together again.
And for you, young man, I have a reading too.
You know I don't believe in any of this.
It doesn't matter what you believe. My cards never lie.
This card is about reconciliation - about a bond held together by balance.
When one makes the first step - and the other finally responds.
For you it means one thing: stop trying to carry everything alone, and stop hiding behind jokes.
Say what matters - in time - while there's still a bridge between you.
And one more thing. The Two of Cups comes when roads diverge... but the meeting is already set.
For me, these are nothing more than just words.
What needs to happen will happen.
This card is about reconciliation. But not necessarily about love.
About the hand that's hard to offer first. And the conversation you've put off for too long.
Is this somehow connected to my father?
Listen further.
Say what you must say - to the one you've owed it to for a long time.
And also... the Two of Cups often appears when a person chooses the road back.
Not to return to the past, but to walk through it properly and open a path forward.
Sometimes, to find the one who disappeared, you first have to stop losing those who are still beside you.
